draft.title: Paragraph organisation and meaning
card: Authors choose where to place an idea. The same idea can have a different effect on the reader depending on its position.
an idea placed at the start of a paragraph or text gets attention straight away. It can set the main point or the mood for what follows.
an idea placed at the end is the one the reader has just read. It can leave a lasting impression or push the reader to act or think.
Ideas in the middle can build on the first idea, give evidence, or lead the reader towards the final point.
draft.remember: Position shapes effect: first grabs attention, last is what the reader carries away.

a.q: An article about a school garden ends with its strongest idea: every student should help. What is the effect of placing it last?
opts: It leaves a lasting impression on the reader
It makes the idea seem less important
It sets the mood before the topic begins
It hides the idea among the supporting points
a.why: The last idea is the one the reader has just read, so it tends to stay in mind. It does not hide the idea or set the mood at the start, because those effects come from other positions.
a.clue: What does a reader remember just after finishing?

b.q: Jin writes a speech about water safety. He opens with a shocking fact about drownings in Queensland. Why might he place it first?
opts: To catch attention and set the main concern straight away
To let the audience forget it by the end of the speech
To act as a quiet link between two supporting points
To leave the audience with a final call to action
b.why: An idea placed first gets attention straight away and can set the main point. Placing it first does not make it a final call to action, because that effect belongs to the end of a text.
b.clue: Think about what the audience hears before anything else.

a.best: It leaves a lasting impression on the reader

b.best: To catch attention and set the main concern straight away
